title: @origingame/engine API v1
description:
The Origin Engine API. Game code declares components and systems, and reads the world through typed views over engine memory.
Every failure is a returned Result; desc objects may omit any field; nothing reads the wall clock inside a tick.

x-og-units.cssPx: CSS pixels of the play surface, origin at the top left

x-og-modules.name: math
x-og-modules.doc: Plain math values in the three.js vocabulary. They are data: the engine owns the operations, so results are identical on every host.

x-og-modules.name: reflect
x-og-modules.doc:
Reflection: components and resources are declared once with their field layout and metadata, and registered by name.
The inspector, Tune, the probe, scene text and the wiki read this one schema. Each column factory below makes one field.

functions.name: defineComponent
functions.doc:
Declare a component: plain data stored per entity in engine memory, one column per field.
Registration is by name, so a hot reload re-registers the same component and migrates its fields by name.

params.name: name
params.doc: The component's unique name, PascalCase, as it appears in scenes and dumps.

params.name: fields
params.doc: The layout: field names to column factories, as `{ hp: f32(100) }`.

functions.returnsDoc: The token systems, queries and the world take.

functions.name: defineResource
functions.doc: Declare a resource: a reflected singleton, such as a tuning table. Its fields start at their defaults.
functions.returnsDoc: The token `world.resource` and system declarations take.

x-og-modules.name: world
x-og-modules.doc:
The world: an archetype ECS. Entities are generational handles; components are columns in engine memory.
Structural changes (spawn, despawn, insert, remove) invalidate typed views; the API refuses a stale view.

interfaces.name: World
interfaces.doc: The world a system, a command or a game callback is handed. Game code never holds a world beyond the call it was passed to.

members.name: tick
members.doc: Fixed steps taken since the world was created.

members.name: spawn
members.doc: Spawn an entity.
members.returnsDoc: The new entity, or why it was refused (a duplicate name, a dead parent).

members.name: despawn
members.doc: Despawn an entity and its descendants.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity.

members.name: alive
members.doc: Whether an entity handle is live.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether an entity has a component.

members.name: insert
members.doc: Add a component to an entity, or overwrite it when present. A structural change.

params.name: value
params.doc: Field values; omitted fields take their defaults.

members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or an unregistered component.

members.name: remove
members.doc: Remove a component from an entity. A structural change.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: get
members.doc: Copy one entity's component value. For bulk work use a system's typed views.

members.name: set
members.doc: Write some fields of one entity's component.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: resource
members.doc: A resource's live value. Inside a system, the resource must be among the system's reads or writes.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for an unregistered resource or one the running system did not declare.

members.name: find
members.doc: The entity with a name.
members.returnsDoc: Null when no live entity has the name.

members.name: nameOf
members.doc: An entity's name.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unnamed or dead entity.

members.name: query
members.doc: A query over the current archetypes, for commands and callbacks; systems receive theirs.

members.name: events
members.doc: The events of one type emitted during the previous tick and this one, oldest first.

members.name: emit
members.doc: Emit an event; readers see it this tick and the next.

members.name: instantiate
members.doc: Spawn a loaded scene or glTF asset into the world as a tree of entities.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Name, parent and transform of the root entity.

members.returnsDoc: The root entity, or why it was refused (an asset still loading, a failed asset).

interfaces.name: Query
interfaces.doc: A set of matched archetypes. Iterate archetypes, never entities one by one.

members.name: archetypes
members.doc: The matched archetypes this tick.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of matched entities.

interfaces.name: ArchetypeView
interfaces.doc: One archetype's columns for this tick. Views are invalidated by structural changes; using a stale view throws with the tick and the system it belonged to.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of entities in the archetype.

members.name: tick
members.doc: The tick this view belongs to.

members.name: entities
members.doc: The entities as (index, generation) pairs: entity i is at 2i and 2i + 1.

members.name: entity
members.doc: The handle of entity i.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether the archetype carries a component.

members.name: column
members.doc:
The typed views of a component's fields: one typed array per field, `count * stride` long.
Writing requires the component among the system's writes; reading among its reads or writes.

x-og-modules.name: system
x-og-modules.doc:
Systems: functions the engine calls once per tick with their matched archetypes.
A system declares what it reads and writes; a write to an undeclared component is refused at registration with the field name.

members.name: name
members.doc: The system's unique name.

members.name: reads
members.doc: What it reads.

members.name: writes
members.doc: What it writes.

callbacks.name: SystemRun
callbacks.doc: A system's body. It is called once per tick; loop over `q.archetypes()`, then over rows.

params.name: q
params.doc: The archetypes matching the declared components.

params.name: time
params.doc: The Time resource for this tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world, for resources, events and structural changes.

x-og-modules.name: game
x-og-modules.doc: The game entry: what the bundle's default export declares.

functions.name: game
functions.doc: Declare the game. The bundle's default export is its result.

interfaces.name: Game
interfaces.doc: A declared game, the bundle's default export.

members.name: tick
members.doc: The fixed tick rate in hertz.

members.name: systems
members.doc: The systems in declaration order.

callbacks.name: FactsFn
callbacks.doc: The game's own facts for the probe's state(): a small JSON object, computed from the world without changing it.

x-og-modules.name: transform
x-og-modules.doc: Transforms in the three.js vocabulary: position, quaternion and scale, composed into matrixWorld down the parent chain.

functions.name: compose
functions.doc: A matrix from position, rotation and scale, as three.js Matrix4.compose.

functions.name: decompose
functions.doc: Position, rotation and scale from a matrix, as three.js Matrix4.decompose.

functions.name: lookAt
functions.doc: The rotation that points -Z from an eye towards a target, as three.js Object3D.lookAt for cameras.

params.name: up
params.doc: The up direction; the zero vector means +Y.

functions.name: fromAxisAngle
functions.doc: A rotation about an axis, as three.js Quaternion.setFromAxisAngle.

x-og-modules.name: time
x-og-modules.doc: Simulation time. Game code never reads the wall clock; it reads Time.

x-og-modules.name: rng
x-og-modules.doc: Deterministic randomness. Every random draw comes from an Rng stream; the sequence for a seed is identical on every host and in the Web scaffold's rng.ts.

interfaces.name: RngStream
interfaces.doc: One generator stream, forked from the Rng resource for a subsystem that must not perturb the main sequence.

members.name: seed
members.doc: The stream's derived seed.

members.name: next
members.doc: Uniform in [0, 1).

members.name: range
members.doc: Uniform in [low, high).

members.name: integer
members.doc: A uniform integer in [low, high].

members.name: chance
members.doc: True with probability p.

members.name: fork
members.doc: A fresh stream on a seed derived from this stream's seed and a label.

params.name: label
params.doc: The subsystem's name; the same label always gives the same stream.

x-og-modules.name: input
x-og-modules.doc:
Input as the game sees it: the Input resource for polling, events for edges.
The shell collects pointer, keyboard and wheel input on the main thread; the probe and the command channel inject through the same path.

x-og-modules.name: camera
x-og-modules.doc: The main camera, as a resource with three.js PerspectiveCamera and OrthographicCamera parameter names.

x-og-modules.name: render
x-og-modules.doc: What is drawn: meshes with materials. Draws are instanced by (geometry, material) automatically; there is no per-object draw call.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameters; omitted ones take three.js defaults.

functions.name: updateMaterial
functions.doc: Change some parameters of a standard material.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameters to change; omitted ones keep their values.

functions.name: capabilities
functions.doc: The renderer's tier and limits on this device.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer is asked.

x-og-modules.name: load
x-og-modules.doc:
Asset loading. Paths are relative to the project and read cooked output; a load returns a handle at once and completes at a tick boundary.
Under og run and in replays every load completes before the next tick, so the tick a load lands on is deterministic.

functions.name: gltf
functions.doc: Load a glTF (.gltf or .glb) through the cook, as three.js GLTFLoader.load.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The source path under assets/, such as `assets/ship.glb`.

functions.returnsDoc: The handle, or why it was refused (an uncooked path, a cook stamp mismatch).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.name: gltfInfo

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pending, failed or non-glTF asset.

x-og-modules.name: commands
x-og-modules.doc:
The command channel: actions scheduled on simulation time, from `og run --commands "t:action[:args];..."` or the probe's commands().
Core actions ship with the engine; a module or a game registers more. Unknown actions warn and continue. Not in publish builds.

functions.name: register
functions.doc: Register an action into the command channel. GameDesc.commands does this for a game's own actions.

params.name: name
params.doc: The action name, snake_case, such as `spawn_wave`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a name a core action or another registration already uses.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: Parse a script without scheduling it.
functions.returnsDoc: The steps, or the first malformed step.

functions.name: schedule
functions.doc: Schedule a script on simulation time, from the current tick.
functions.returnsDoc: The report, or the first malformed step.

callbacks.name: CommandHandler
callbacks.doc: A registered action. It runs at the start of the tick it was scheduled for.

params.name: args
params.doc: The `:`-separated arguments after the action name.

x-og-modules.name: probe
x-og-modules.doc:
The probe: RuntimeProbe protocol 5 (origin/packages/contracts/src/probe.ts) served natively, plus the engine's wire members.
In a page it is published on globalThis.__runtime_probe__; on native, `og` serves it as JSON-RPC 2.0 over a loopback WebSocket at /probe.
A refusal is false or null exactly as protocol 5; a JSON-RPC error is only for a malformed call or an unknown method.
Probe entity ids are entity names; an unnamed entity is `#<index>.<generation>`.

consts.name: PROBE_GLOBAL
consts.doc: The global the page publishes the probe on.

consts.name: PROBE_VERSION
consts.doc: The RuntimeProbe contract revision both sides speak.

consts.name: REPLAY_SEED_PARAM
consts.doc: The page query parameter that starts a deterministic replay from a uint32 seed.

consts.name: PLAYTEST_MAX_TICKS
consts.doc: The longest playtest one request may advance, in fixed steps.

consts.name: PROBE_PROGRAM_MAX_OPERATIONS
consts.doc: The most operations one probe program may carry.

interfaces.name: RuntimeProbe
interfaces.doc: RuntimeProbe protocol 5, member for member. Every member answers synchronously with JSON-serialisable values.

members.name: version
members.doc: PROBE_VERSION.

members.name: tick
members.doc: Fixed steps the world has taken since load.

members.name: state
members.doc: A JSON snapshot: the fixed timings head, then the game's own facts.

members.name: advance
members.doc: Take whole fixed steps regardless of the wall clock.
members.returnsDoc: The tick after the steps.

members.name: pause
members.doc: Hold the wall-clock loop; advance still steps.

members.name: resume
members.doc: Release the wall-clock loop.

members.name: input
members.doc: One event through the input layer's own path.
members.returnsDoc: False is a refusal.

members.name: accepted
members.doc: Page events (keyboard, pointer, wheel) the input layer accepted since load.

members.name: pick
members.doc: What is under a point of the play surface.
members.returnsDoc: Null when nothing is under the point.

members.name: entity
members.doc: One entity's published parameters: its tunable fields as `Component.field` keys.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: bounds
members.doc: The ranges of one entity's tunable fields, from the schema.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: patch
members.doc: Move one tunable field for this run only; it applies within one frame. The probe never writes project files.
members.returnsDoc: False is a refusal.

members.name: run
members.doc: Run a program of the members above in order, stopping at the first refusal.

interfaces.name: EngineProbe
interfaces.doc: The engine's probe: protocol 5 plus the wire members of the loopback WebSocket and the in-page request ring.

members.name: hello
members.doc: Who is speaking: protocol, wire, engine version, tick rate, renderer tier, build.

members.name: capture
members.doc: The frame rendered at the current tick, read back offscreen.

params.name: width
params.doc: Width in pixels; 0 is the render target's.

params.name: height
params.doc: Height in pixels; 0 is the render target's.

members.returnsDoc: Null without a renderer.

members.name: sweep
members.doc: A filmstrip over one tunable: per value, restore, patch, advance, capture.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameter, values, steps and size.

members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity or parameter, or without a renderer.

members.name: reload
members.doc: Hot reload: snapshot, swap the game bundle, re-register components by name, restore.
members.returnsDoc: Null when the new bundle fails to load; the old one keeps running.

members.name: snapshot
members.doc: Snapshot the whole world in the running process.

members.name: restore
members.doc: Restore a snapshot taken by this process.
members.returnsDoc: False for an unknown id.

members.name: dump
members.doc: A world, entity or UI dump, as the command channel's dump actions write.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: commands
members.doc: Schedule a command script on simulation time, as `og run --commands`.
members.returnsDoc: Null for a malformed script.

Vector3.description: A 3D vector, as three.js Vector3. The engine is right-handed with +Y up, as three.js.

Quaternion.description: A unit quaternion rotation, as three.js Quaternion. The zero value is the identity.

Matrix4.description: A 4x4 matrix, as three.js Matrix4: sixteen elements in column-major order. The zero value is the identity.

elements.description: The elements, column-major, as three.js Matrix4.elements.

Color.description: A linear RGB colour, as three.js Color with colour management on. Components are usually between 0 and 1; above 1 is HDR.

direction.description: The unit direction the ray points in.

FieldOptions.description: Metadata of one field. Ranges and units are what Tune and the probe's bounds show; nothing clamps writes.

unit.description: A unit name from the API's unit table, or empty.

label.description: The person-facing name; empty uses the field name.

doc.description: One sentence on what the field means.

tunable.description: Publish the field to Tune and to the probe's bounds and patch.

Entity.description:
An entity: an index and a generation. The value is index + generation * 2^32, with the generation below 2^21, so it stays an exact JavaScript number.
Generations start at 1, so 0 is never a live entity.

SpawnDesc.description: How to spawn an entity. `{}` spawns an unnamed entity at the origin with a Transform.

name.description: A unique name; the probe and the command channel address the entity by it. Empty leaves it unnamed.

parent.description: The parent entity; the new entity's Transform is then relative to it.

bare.description: Spawn without a Transform: a pure data entity.

without.description: Components an entity must not have.

SystemDesc.description: A system's declared access and order.

reads.description: Components and resources the system reads. Components here also shape its query.

writes.description: Components and resources the system writes. Components here also shape its query.

without.description: Components a matched entity must not have.

after.description: Names of systems that must run before this one.

before.description: Names of systems that must run after this one.

GameDesc.description: A game: its tick, scenes, systems and commands.

seed.description: The project seed every Rng stream derives from. A replay overrides it.

scenes.description: Scene names to `.ogt` paths, as `{ main: "scenes/main.ogt" }`.

systems.description: The systems, in declaration order before `after`/`before` constraints apply.

resources.description: The game's own resources, created at their defaults.

commands.description: Game actions registered into the command channel, by action name.

maxCatchUp.description: The most ticks one frame may run to catch up with the clock; the accumulator drops the rest.

facts.description: The game's own facts for the probe's state().

Transform.description: Where an entity is, relative to its parent (or the world).

Parent.description: The entity this one's Transform is relative to. Set by SpawnDesc.parent.

MatrixWorld.description: The world matrix the engine composes after the systems run, as three.js Object3D.matrixWorld.

Time.description: The fixed tick's clock. Every value is a function of the tick count, so a replay sees the same numbers.

dt.description: The length of one tick: 1 / rate.

elapsed.description: Simulation time since load: tick * dt.

Rng.description: The world's main random stream, seeded from GameDesc.seed (or the replay seed). Its state is part of every snapshot.

seed.description: The seed the stream started from.

state.description: The generator state; snapshot and restore carry it.

KeyAction.description: What an injected key event does.

x-og-variants.press: Down, then up on the next tick.

PointerAction.description: What an injected pointer event does.

x-og-variants.click: Down, then up on the next tick, at the point.

PointerButton.description: A physical pointer button; `none` is a hover move.

x-og-variants.left: The primary button, or a touch.

Modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during a key event.

platform.description: Command on macOS, the Windows key on Windows.

KeyInput.description: A key event. `key` names the physical key as KeyboardEvent.code does: ArrowRight, Space, KeyA.

PointerInput.description: A pointer event at a point in CSS pixels of the play surface.

button.description: The button; `none` for a hover move.

WheelInput.description: A wheel or trackpad scroll at a point.

InjectedInput.description: One input event in the game's own vocabulary, as the probe's input() and playtest scripts carry it.

button.description: The button; `none` for a hover move.

Input.description: The input state at the start of this tick. Edges (pressed, released) last exactly one tick.

pointerInside.description: Whether the pointer is over the play surface.

Camera.description: The camera the frame is rendered from. Rendering reads it after the tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.

quaternion.description: Its rotation; the camera looks down its local -Z.

fov.description: The vertical field of view of the perspective projection.

zoom.description: The zoom factor, as three.js Camera.zoom.

orthographic.description: Use an orthographic projection (the 2D profile) instead of a perspective one.

height.description: The visible world height of the orthographic projection.

background.description: The clear colour, as three.js Scene.background. The default is the brand ink #14161b in linear RGB.

exposure.description: Exposure before tone mapping, as three.js toneMappingExposure.

Geometry.description: Vertex and index data, as three.js BufferGeometry. Comes from a loaded glTF.

Side.description: Which faces are drawn, as three.js FrontSide, BackSide and DoubleSide.

RenderTier.description: The backend the renderer runs on; the probe's hello reports it.

x-og-variants.webgpu: WebGPU in a browser: the full feature set.
x-og-variants.webgl2: The WebGL2 fallback: no compute, CPU culling and particles, tiled lights.
x-og-variants.vulkan: Native Vulkan, on lavapipe or a GPU.
x-og-variants.none: No renderer: frames are not produced and capture refuses.

StandardMaterialDesc.description: A physically based metallic-roughness material with three.js MeshStandardMaterial parameter names.

metalnessMap.description: Metalness from the texture's blue channel.

roughnessMap.description: Roughness from the texture's green channel.

aoMap.description: Ambient occlusion from the texture's red channel.

emissiveIntensity.description: A multiplier on the emitted colour.

opacity.description: The opacity; below 1 only with transparent.

transparent.description: Blend instead of writing opaque pixels.

alphaTest.description: Discard pixels whose alpha is below this.

Mesh.description: Draws a geometry with a material at the entity's MatrixWorld, as a three.js Mesh.

RenderCapabilities.description: What the renderer can do on this device. Backend limits are reported here, never by missing members.

compute.description: Whether compute passes run (GPU culling, GPU particles).

maxShadowedLights.description: How many lights may cast shadows.

width.description: The render target width in device pixels.

height.description: The render target height in device pixels.

Asset.description: A loaded scene or glTF asset.

x-og-variants.failed: Failed; the AssetFailed event carries the reason.

GltfDesc.description: How to load a glTF, as three.js GLTFLoader options where they apply.

castShadow.description: Set Mesh.castShadow on every mesh instantiated from it.

receiveShadow.description: Set Mesh.receiveShadow on every mesh instantiated from it.

geometries.description: Its geometries, in glTF mesh-primitive order.

path.description: The path it was loaded from.
The path it was loaded from.

CoreAction.description: The actions the engine ships. Arguments follow the action, separated by `:`.

x-og-variants.touch_move_to: `touch_move_to:<ui id>`: move the pointer to a UI element.
x-og-variants.touch_move: `touch_move:x,y`: move the pointer to CSS pixel coordinates.
x-og-variants.touch_start: `touch_start`: press the pointer where it is.
x-og-variants.key_down: `key_down:<Key>`: hold a key by its code.
x-og-variants.type: `type:<text>`: type text, one key press per character.
x-og-variants.move_to_text: `move_to_text:[=]text[@N]`: move the pointer to the UI element showing the text (exactly with `=`, the Nth with `@N`).
x-og-variants.frame_entity: `frame_entity:<entity>`: point the camera at an entity.
x-og-variants.dump_world: `dump_world[:path]`: tables, systems and their matched counts.
x-og-variants.set: `set:<entity>.<component>.<field>=<value>`: a Tune write through the schema.
x-og-variants.pause: `pause`: hold the clock; advance still steps.

CommandDesc.description: How a registered action describes itself in `og run --help` and the wiki.

doc.description: One sentence on what it does.

CommandStep.description: One parsed step of a command script.

at.description: When it runs, in simulation seconds from the start of the script.

untilTick.description: The tick of the last step.

warnings.description: Unknown actions and other skipped steps, each naming the fix.

PickResult.description: What a screen point resolved to.

entity.description: The probe id of the entity under the point.

world.description: Where the pick landed in world space: two components in the 2D profile, three in 3D; nothing pads a plane with an unmeasured zero.

source.description: Where a person would change it, as `player.ts::jump`.

ProbeTunable.description: One published tunable parameter and the range it means something over.

ProbeEntityRef.description: One entity the probe publishes in state().

ProbeTimings.description: The fixed timings head of state().

render.description: Time the last frame's render took; 0 without a renderer.

ProbeState.description: The probe's state(): a fixed head, then the game's own facts.

seed.description: The seed the world was assembled from.

ProbeOperation.description: One operation of a probe program, which runs in one evaluation so a scripted segment costs one round trip.

oneOf.description: Take fixed steps; answers the tick.
Read the state; answers `{ tick, state }`.
Pick a point; answers its result or null.
Read an entity's parameters; null is a refusal.

ProbeProgramResult.description: What a program observed: one answer per operation that ran. A false, or entity's null, stops the program and `refused` names its index.

refused.description: The index of the refusing operation, or null.

tick.description: The tick after the last operation that ran.

Hello.description: The wire's hello: who is speaking.

members.description: The probe members this build serves.

BuildProfile.description: The build configuration; publish builds keep only the player-facing probe members.

x-og-variants.dev: A development build: every member, the command channel, dumps.
x-og-variants.release: An optimised build with every member.
x-og-variants.publish: A published game: hello, tick, state, pick, entity, input and capture only.

SweepDesc.description: A parameter sweep: for each value, restore the snapshot taken at the call, patch, advance and capture.

id.description: The probe id of the entity.

values.description: The values to try, in order.

steps.description: Fixed steps to advance after each patch.

width.description: Capture width; 0 is the render target's.

height.description: Capture height; 0 is the render target's.

SweepResult.description: A sweep's frames, one per value.

ReloadReport.description: What a hot reload did. Components are re-registered by name and migrated field by field through the schema.

tick.description: The tick the world was restored at.

ms.description: From bundle swap to restored world.

migrated.description: Fields carried across a layout change, as `Health.hp`.

dropped.description: Components or fields that no longer exist, dropped with their data.

warnings.description: Anything else worth reading, each naming the fix.

SnapshotInfo.description: A snapshot of the whole world (components, resources, Rng states, pending events) kept in the running process.

tick.description: The tick it was taken at.

hash.description: The world hash at that tick, hex: equal hashes mean equal worlds.

x-og-variants.world: Archetype tables, systems and their matched counts.

id.description: The probe id, for an entity dump.

matched.description: Entities its query matched on the last tick.

ms.description: Time it took on the last tick.

components.description: Each component's field values, by component name.

UiElement.description: One UI element with its bounds.

id.description: Its stable id, as the command channel targets it.

parent.description: Its parent's id; empty at the root.

text.description: The text it shows, if any.

UiDump.description: The UI tree, flattened in draw order.

DumpResult.description: A dump, tagged by its kind.

components.description: Each component's field values, by component name.
